use: Merrow Lane Partners, an eleven-person private-equity firm buying software companies valued between $2M and $15M, will retain Tuuyi's claims-review service at the attested tier, first for a $4.2M purchase of a scheduling-software company and then, if that goes well, for roughly six deals a year. The firm's vice-president for technical diligence runs the engagement; the firm's own engineer opens and confirms the citations in the report. The firm has listed six things it is paying for — claims frozen before testing, citations its engineer can confirm, an independent second check, ratings against its stated thresholds, a person's signature, and the seller's code kept on hardware Tuuyi controls — and three conditions that would end the deal outright. It needs the report within 10 days of the seller uploading the code, inside a 21-day exclusivity period, and its investment committee may ask to see the working record as much as a year later.

items.item: Listing every seller claim and freezing the list before any testing
items.if_it_failed: If claims could be added or changed after testing began, the firm could not trust that the report covers the whole claim set, and its engineer would have to reconstruct the list from the seller's documents — costly for an eleven-person firm inside a 10-day window.
items.buyer_words: every seller claim listed and frozen before testing

items.item: Testing each frozen claim against the target's code, configuration and build files
items.if_it_failed: If the claims were not actually tested against the code, the firm's engineer would have to do that code-reading deal by deal themselves; this is the core of what is being bought, not something a competent engineer replaces in a day, so the cost would be heavy.
items.buyer_words: every finding cited to a file and line that the firm's own engineer can open and confirm

items.item: Citing every finding to a file and line the firm's engineer can open and confirm
items.if_it_failed: If findings were not cited this way, the firm could not verify the review's work itself and would have to take it on trust or commission its own diligence; it cannot repair that cheaply given who it said will operate the offering.
items.buyer_words: every finding cited to a file and line that the firm's own engineer can open and confirm

items.item: Mechanically catching citations that do not resolve before anyone reads the report
items.if_it_failed: The firm's engineer would have to check each citation by hand before the report went to the committee, which is slow work against the 10-day need and repeated at every deal.
items.buyer_words: citations that are not verified mechanically as the website says

items.item: An independent second check of every finding, done without re-using the first reader's conclusions
items.if_it_failed: If the check were skipped for some findings or re-used the first reader's work, the firm would be paying for a single reading; it cannot repair this itself and would have to discount the report or stop using the service.
items.buyer_words: every finding checked a second time independently ... an independent check that re-uses the first reader's conclusions or is skipped for some findings

items.item: Materiality and exposure ratings made against the thresholds the firm states
items.if_it_failed: If ratings ignored the firm's stated thresholds, the materiality judgements would be meaningless to the investment committee; the firm would have to re-weight the findings itself, which it cannot credibly do without the very skill it is buying.
items.buyer_words: ratings made against the thresholds the firm states ... a rating step that does not use the firm's stated thresholds

items.item: A person's signature on the conclusion, with human judgement distinguishable from machine work
items.if_it_failed: The firm cannot repair this; if a step the website describes as done by a person were done by the tooling alone, the report's authority with the committee would fail and the price would not be justified.
items.buyer_words: a person's signature on the conclusion ... a step the website describes as done by a person that is done by the tooling alone, or the reverse

items.item: The seller's code kept on hardware Tuuyi controls on paid engagements, never reaching a cloud model service or any other party
items.if_it_failed: This ends the deal: the firm's non-disclosure agreements with sellers forbid passing seller code to any third party other than a named adviser, and no repair is possible once a disclosure has happened.
items.buyer_words: any of a seller's code reaching a cloud model service or any party other than Tuuyi on a paid engagement ... the seller's code kept on hardware Tuuyi controls

items.item: Seller materials visible to no one but the seller and the practice
items.if_it_failed: This ends the deal; a leak to any other eyes would breach the firm's obligations to its sellers and cannot be undone.
items.buyer_words: the seller's materials being visible to anyone but the seller and the practice

items.item: The firm's deal terms held only in the engagement file
items.if_it_failed: This ends the deal; the firm stated this as a condition of any paid engagement and cannot repair a storage practice on Tuuyi's side.
items.buyer_words: the firm's deal terms being stored anywhere other than the engagement file

items.item: The report arriving within 10 days of the seller uploading the code
items.if_it_failed: The firm would have to negotiate a longer exclusivity period or drop the review from the deal; with exclusivity already short, this is costly and may not be achievable.
items.buyer_words: the firm needs the report in hand within 10 days of the seller uploading the code ... a turnaround longer than the website states, because the exclusivity period is short

items.item: The working record being kept, so any finding can be traced back to its searches and files a year later
items.if_it_failed: If the record were not kept, the firm could not answer its investment committee's later questions; it cannot reconstruct a record it never held, and the report alone would not carry the traceability it is paying for.
items.buyer_words: the working record not being kept, because the committee may ask for it a year later

items.item: The engagement-site page where the seller uploads the materials, open only to the seller and the practice
items.if_it_failed: If the upload page failed, the firm could supply the materials by another arrangement with Tuuyi, since the firm itself never has to handle the code; a workable workaround, though it would eat some of the 10 days.
items.buyer_words: within 10 days of the seller uploading the code

items.item: A fresh examination environment provisioned per paid engagement and deleted when it ends
items.if_it_failed: If environments were shared between deals or not torn down, one seller's code could survive into another engagement, breaching the firm's walk-away condition; the firm cannot repair Tuuyi's infrastructure and would have to stop using the service.
items.buyer_words: the seller's code kept on hardware Tuuyi controls

items.item: The intake conversation that records who the firm is, what it is evaluating, and its thresholds
items.if_it_failed: If intake failed to capture the firm's thresholds, the ratings step would have nothing to rate against; the firm would have to restate them before the review could proceed, which is feasible but delays a timetable that is already tight.
items.buyer_words: ratings made against the thresholds the firm states

items.item: How the intake page is built and how long intake takes
items.if_it_failed: No effect on the firm's plan, provided the report still arrives inside the 10 days.
items.buyer_words: it does not care how the intake page is built or how long intake takes, so long as the report arrives inside the 10 days

items.item: The free demo and its question-answering interface
items.if_it_failed: No effect; the firm ran the demo once and will not use it again, though it still expects the demo to be described honestly on the website.
items.buyer_words: the free demo and the developer beta are of no commercial interest to the firm, and that it will never use them again

items.item: The developer beta and the free beta review path that runs on a hosted model
items.if_it_failed: No effect; the firm will never use it, and the hosted model it runs on touches none of the firm's own engagements.
items.buyer_words: the free demo and the developer beta are of no commercial interest to the firm, and that it will never use them again

items.item: The stated limits of the review — not a penetration test, not a code-quality review, not legal advice
items.if_it_failed: No effect on the plan; the firm buys nothing in those categories from Tuuyi and covers them through other advisers.
items.buyer_words: it has no view on the limits the website states (not a penetration test, not a code-quality review, not legal advice); it has other advisers for those

items.item: Runtime claims reported unsettled rather than verified, since nothing is compiled or executed
items.if_it_failed: If the review did not flag clearly what it could not settle and instead implied more than the evidence shows, the firm's engineer would have to test runtime behaviour deal by deal — costly for an eleven-person firm on a 10-day timetable.
items.buyer_words: every finding cited to a file and line that the firm's own engineer can open and confirm

items.item: The private question page for asking about the delivered report, drawing on the working record, available for the life of the decision
items.if_it_failed: The firm would fall back on the report and its own copy of the record to answer committee questions; an irritation rather than a failure, since the record itself is what it is chiefly paying to have kept.
items.buyer_words: the committee may ask for it a year later

items.item: Findings issued at delivery staying unmodified, with no quiet rewriting afterwards
items.if_it_failed: If issued findings were quietly changed, the year-old record the committee may consult would no longer match the report; the firm cannot repair this itself and would have to demand frozen, dated deliveries.
items.buyer_words: the committee may ask for it a year later

items.item: Each frozen claim producing its own finding with a verdict, with both sides of a partly-true result preserved
items.if_it_failed: Without a stated status for each claim, the report would be a pile of evidence with no conclusions; the price would not be justified and the firm could not supply the missing judgement itself.
items.buyer_words: every finding cited to a file and line that the firm's own engineer can open and confirm

items.item: The attested tier's practitioner being available to the firm's deal team through closing
items.if_it_failed: The buyer has not said; a person should ask.
items.buyer_words: the live deal's exclusivity period ends in 21 days

items.item: The engagement letter setting the terms, retention and limitation of liability, one review at a time
items.if_it_failed: If the letter did not govern as described, the firm would have to settle terms before the first engagement; that is doable before paying and cheap at this stage, but it must happen.
items.buyer_words: a service engagement under Tuuyi's engagement letter, one review at a time, no retainer

items.item: The founder's stated credentials — due diligence done from both sides of deals, and that he personally signs the attested reviews
items.if_it_failed: If the credentials were not as described, the signature the firm is paying for would carry less weight; the firm cannot repair that and would have to weigh the report on its citations alone before continuing to the further five deals a year.
items.buyer_words: a person's signature on the conclusion

items.item: The division of labour: the firm names the claim documents and supplies the deal context, may add claims of its own, and never receives the code
items.if_it_failed: If the service demanded materials or deal assumptions the firm had not agreed to supply, the firm's vice-president would have to renegotiate the workflow before the review could start — feasible but disruptive to the 10-day need.
items.buyer_words: one attested review on a live deal (a $4.2M purchase of a scheduling-software company)

items.item: The public website's own visitor-facing behaviour — the contact form and its bot check, the absence of cookies and analytics on the public pages
items.if_it_failed: The buyer has not said; a person should ask.
